concepts.why: Secular scholar / Reformed reader: the renamed concept says the life of every living thing is in His hand. Ps 147:8-9 says only that He prepares rain, grows grass and provides food for animals; it names neither life nor His hand (unlike Job 12:10, Neh 9:6, Ps 104:28-30, Ps 145:16, Acts 17:25), so the name says more than this passage. The drafter's 'instance of the same provision' is the drafter's grouping, not the text's.

Secular scholar and Reformed/Baptist readers: the name is 'Let them praise the name of the LORD' (Ps 148:5, 13). Isa 55:12 does not mention praise or the LORD; its mountains and trees break into song and clap before the people who go out in joy and peace, so it is not the same statement and shares only the image of rejoicing nature. Ps 96:11-12 and 98:7-8 also say 'rejoice/sing for joy' rather than 'praise' and are cut off before 'before the LORD' (96:13, 98:9); kept as the same call to the sea, fields and mountains, but the drafter could extend each by its next verse if the LORD is to appear in the cited text (that adds 'He is coming to judge', so leaving them as they are is the cleaner choice).

secondary_or_links: Secondary 'The tree of life -> in the middle of the garden': the arrow is not what most of the verses say. Only Gen 2:9 has 'in the middle of the garden'; Gen 3:22 and 3:24 say take and eat / the way to the tree of life, Rev 2:7 and 22:14 say the right to eat from / the right to the tree of life, and Rev 22:2 says down the middle of the main street of the city. Change the arrow to 'the way to the tree of life' (Gen 3:24; Rev 22:14) or drop the arrow to the bare name; do not keep 'in the middle of the garden' over Revelation.

Secondary 'By wisdom -> the earth founded': Proverbs 8:27-30 runs on into v30 ('I was a skilled craftsman at His side'), which no concept here needs and which is exactly where Nicene and Arian, Jewish and Christian readers part on who Wisdom is. Cut to Proverbs 8:27-29 (the earth's foundations are in v29).

Concept 12 passage Hebrews 1:2-3 runs on to 'sat down at the right hand of the Majesty', which the concept does not need; trim to 1:2-3 up to 'upholding all things by His powerful word' if the drafter's tool allows a partial verse, otherwise leave as is (minor, not a ground for revising the concept).
Links: the list reads correctly; Law/Wisdom and Wisdom Literature resting on different passages is accepted as the drafter explains. No change.
